mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a short-term negative reaction in S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not diverge significantly from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 1.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 4.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days due to increased labor market rigidity and reduced consumer spending expectations.
regime_hint: rising unemployment or tight labor market
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive months where UNRATE > 4.5%, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP demand proxy GDPC1 exceeds INDPRO by more than 10 percentage points, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days are expected to be positive, reflecting excess demand and upward price pressure.
failure_condition: Across 10 such demand gap events, 20-day rolling average forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 5 percentage points for three consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to reduced production capacity and upward pricing pressure.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >= 5% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes meeting the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL below 200 (index 1982-1984=100) followed by a subsequent rise signals a disinflationary shock that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 200 and rising in the following month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns after such CPIAUCSL events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 by 20% from the prior month, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days are predicted to be positive due to stronger labor market confidence and corporate optimism.
failure_condition: In 10 such events, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of RSAFS and HOUST above 500 and 1000 respectively signals robust industrial and consumer demand, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: During 5 such events, 20-day rolling average forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for two consecutive months in a labor market cooling regime, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days are expected to be negative due to reduced wage growth and muted consumer spending.
failure_condition: In 5 such cooling regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1).
